uncited: It enables direct manipulation segmentation by computing the corresponding seed voxel from screen coordinates [Parent].

It differs from its siblings by focusing on the inverse lookup from packed framebuffer indices to logical volume coordinates, whereas [Ray-Box Intersection for Interaction](2638-ray-box-intersection-for-interaction.md) computes geometric intersections and [BrushController](2362-brushcontroller.md) manages interaction state.
**Inputs:** Fragment location in the framebuffer ($F$), current slice z-offset ($Z_{offset}$).
*   **Reverse Index Texture:** Maps packed coordinates ($P$) to volume coordinates ($V$).
The texture stores the volume coordinate corresponding to each packed index.
It is chosen when ray integration requires accessing scalar data from a packed volume representation, complementing the Reverse Index Map which is used for initial voxel selection.
*   Do not use when geometric intersection is required instead of index-based lookup [Sibling: Ray-Box Intersection for Interaction].
